mechanism_reading.mach_send_invalid_dest: osfmk/mach/message.h defines MACH_SEND_INVALID_DEST as 0x10000003, and the ports and filedesc logs print it with %#x. send_resource_violation_with_fatal_port logs that return from the caller. host_get_special_port returns KERN_SUCCESS after copying the special-port slot, including an empty slot, and a failed host_get returns before the MIG send. The value 0x10000003 is therefore the send to a bogus destination, which is the comment on MACH_SEND_INVALID_DEST. An empty HOST_RESOURCE_NOTIFY_PORT slot is the path that produces a null destination; a dead destination produces the same send error.
mechanism_reading.ast_order: ast.c 387-391 clears AST_PROC_RESOURCE and calls task_port_space_ast, then proc_filedesc_ast. The captured times are ports caught at 126.273420, ports error at 126.273436, fds caught at 126.273441, and the filedesc error at 126.273491. The ports function prints both of its lines before the filedesc function starts. proc_filedesc_ast returns after an fd notification and does not evaluate kqworkloops; the capture has no kqworkloop line. The order fits one AST_PROC_RESOURCE pass.
mechanism_reading.soft_hard: The log text is fixed per resource. task.c logs send_resource_violation(ports, ...) for both the soft and hard port branches, and send_resource_violation_with_fatal_port(filedesc, ...) for both file-descriptor branches. Those strings are in the booted kernel at macho offsets 1295050 and 1295467. A fatal port is allocated only when hard_limit > 0 (task.c 8690 and 8801). The soft branch passes MACH_PORT_NULL and does not call task_self_sigkill. The four lines do not say which notification carried the fatal port. OS_REASON_SIGNAL code 9 fits a hard-limit fatal-port release on at least one of the two resources. A both-soft reading of these functions would need some other SIGKILL path, and these lines do not show one.
mechanism_reading.limits: Arming uses a strict greater-than test (ipc_space.c 524-530, kern_descrip.c 1187-1193). The notification uses greater-or-equal and logs the current size (ipc_space_check_table_size_limit 599-610, proc_evaluate_fd_limits_ast 5532-5541). The port limit treated as crossed is at most 3. The file-descriptor limit treated as crossed is at most 4. 'Below 3' is the reading if the port count did not fall between the arming check and the log. The kernel applies a limit only when the value is greater than 0. task_set_port_space_limits has one caller, kern_exec.c 5365-5367, and only when a spawn attribute limit is greater than 0. ipc_space_alloc uses Z_ZERO, and fork does not copy port limits. File-descriptor limits are copied in fdt_fork (kern_descrip.c 899-905) and overwritten by spawn attributes (kern_exec.c 5370-5372). The log name comes from proc_name_address, which returns p_comm, so chonk-terminal-d is the 16-character p_comm while the kcdata PROCNAME is the full chonk-terminal-darwin. The kernel format string contains a tab (bytes 20 09 20 20 20 20 between 'ports.' and 'Num'); the captured line has '?' in the tab's place. The spawn-attribute bytes were not recorded. A parent file-descriptor hard limit of 4 or less is a poor fit, because pid 13 stayed up and spawned pid 14, and the parent's open-fd count was not recorded.
mechanism_reading.d4_and_the_record: The record's D4 confirmed sentence matches the criteria string, and that condition is met. The further chain, that the notification path killed pid 14, fits one hard fatal-port release together with the signal reason. The lines still do not identify which resource carried the fatal port. The record already leaves that split, and the spawn-attribute byte values, unclaimed.

facts_record_check.claim: pid 14 had a Mach-port limit below 3 and a file-descriptor limit at or below 4, and nothing in pinned XNU sets these limits except posix_spawn attributes or fork inheritance of the parent's fd limits
facts_record_check.evidence: The logged sizes make the crossed port limit at most 3 and the crossed fd limit at most 4. 'Below 3' needs the count not to have dropped after the strict-greater arming check. Port limits are zero-filled at ipc-space allocation and are not fork-inherited; the only setter is the spawn-attribute path when the value is greater than 0. File-descriptor limits are fork-copied and can be overwritten by spawn attributes. The record already says the attribute bytes were not recorded and that inheritance of the desktop's fd limits is not excluded.
